terms.meaning: the share of users who come back a set number of days after first using the app
the group of users who first appeared in the same week
a fixed world time standard used to avoid time zone differences
a week that runs Monday to Sunday

sections.name: KpiEvent
sections.title: Event shape and day length
sections.what: Describes one analytics event: who did it, the event name, its extra details, and when. It also sets the length of one day in milliseconds.
sections.why: Likely reason: a plain shape lets the calculations run on any list of events.

sections.name: weekStart, Rate, rate
sections.title: Week start and rate helper
sections.what: Finds the Monday at midnight UTC for the week containing a date, and turns a count and a base into a rate. A base of zero gives a missing value, not zero percent.
sections.why: Likely reason: a missing value stops an empty week from showing a misleading zero.
sections.watch_out: Weeks start on Monday in UTC, so a user's local day can fall into a different week.

sections.name: WeeklyKpis
sections.title: Weekly summary shape
sections.what: Lists the fields of one week's summary: active users plus nine rates, including review to next read, retention at 7 and 30 days, and share rate per reveal.
sections.why: Likely reason: one fixed shape gives every reader the same structure.
sections.watch_out: Renaming or adding a field here means every reader of the summary must change too.

sections.name: usersWith
sections.title: Users who did an event
sections.what: Collects the distinct users who logged a named event, optionally only those events that pass an extra test.
sections.why: Likely reason: many measures ask who did something in a week, so this avoids repeating the same filter.
sections.watch_out: Events without a user are skipped.

sections.name: weeklyKpis
sections.title: Computing the weekly summary
sections.what: Works out the week's measures from the event history: who was active, who graded calls and came back to read more, how many new fans locked a call within a week, and whether fans returned at 7 and 30 days. Retention only counts fans whose full window has passed by the given time.
sections.why: Likely reason: the file says the definitions come from a product spec, so the code follows that document.
sections.watch_out: The input must include all earlier history, or first-seen dates and retention will be wrong.

summary: Works out the weekly key numbers for the product from the analytics event log.
purpose: Turns raw analytics events into weekly measures such as activity, returns, and retention.
why: Likely reason: pure calculations with no database access are easy to test and to repeat.
how: 1. Find the Monday that starts the week. 2. Keep events in that week. 3. Count distinct users for each measure. 4. Use earlier history to find first sightings and retention. 5. Return each rate, with a missing value when its base is zero.
inputs: All analytics events up to a date, a week start date, and a current time.
outputs: A weekly summary with the active user count and nine rates.
risks: Missing history gives wrong first-seen dates and retention. Weeks use UTC, so users in other time zones can appear in a different week.
debug: If a rate looks wrong, check its base, since zero shows as missing. Check that the input contains earlier history. Compare the definitions with the product spec named in the file header.
